newsitem.title: UK: HGCA says cereal quality good, but too much supply.
newsitem.headline: HGCA says cereal quality good, but too much supply.

text.p: New samples obtained from this year's UK cereal harvest point to a reasonably good quality crop, the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Tuesday.
But it warned in its latest weekly digest that the bumper harvest, combined with carryover stocks from last year would continue to put pressure on prices.
The average quality results for wheat suggested a similar specific weight to last year at 77.9 kilos per hectolitre and a Hagberg number of 310.
But protein content, particularly on breadmaking wheat, was significantly lower at 10.2 percent.
Barley did well on quality, with the exception of high small grains content for some varieties.
Average specific weight was around 69 kilos per hectolitre and nitrogen content around 1.85-1.90 percent.

The HGCA, quoting data collected by the Ministry of Agriculture (MAFF), reckoned that supplies would be further swollen by large carryover stocks from last year as farmers stocked crops in the hope that prices would rise.

"Unless the sharply increased supplies are matched by substantially larger exports and domestic use, end-season stocks could again be large and seem likely to include some intervention stocks," the HGCA said.
Stocks of wheat were estimated at 750,000 tonnes at end-June, up from 180,000 tonnes the year before, while barley was put at 130,000 tonnes, up from just 20,000 tonnes in 1995.
